hypothesis: Theorems AF-1 and AF-2 predict, on the 4-bit Boolean world with the shared-through-Z task family, that the Pareto frontier over (task-sufficiency, coding cost, dynamical closure, control regret) is a two-element antichain {constant, joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3})}: the constant map is the min-coding-cost endpoint, the CSS Z is the unique zero-task-sufficiency member on the frontier, and the identity is strictly dominated by Z in the static case where the two closure/regret axes are constant.

controls.description: The reference partition Z is computed directly from the ground-truth latent map latent_z(x) = (x_0 ^ x_1, x_2 ^ x_3), independent of any candidate quotient.
weakly_dominates is verified by construction: it is irreflexive (a quotient never dominates itself since strict-on-one fails) and monotone under axis-wise inequalities.

The dynamical_closure and control_regret axes are documented as constants (0) in this static example and cannot spuriously separate quotients; the effective Pareto reduces to (task_sufficiency, coding_cost).

gates.criterion: No two Pareto-set members weakly dominate each other on all four axes with strict inequality on at least one.
joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) is a member of the Pareto frontier.
The constant map is a member of the Pareto frontier.
The identity is strictly dominated by joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}): both have task-sufficiency 0, and Z has strictly smaller coding cost.
Among Pareto members with task-sufficiency 0, the only quotient is joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}).
No Pareto member is strictly finer than joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) on the lattice; equivalently, the identity (the only strictly finer library element) is not on the frontier.
